transcript:
Header:
- Date: 2026-04-07
- Time: 10:00 AM PT
- Duration: 45 minutes
- Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Kapoor (Redwood SE), Ethan Morales (Redwood SA); Maya Chen (Atlas Head of ML), Luis Ortega (Atlas Infra Lead), Samir Patel (Atlas CTO)

Auto-summary: quick benchmark review comparing Redwood runtime to Atlas's baseline provider. Some noisy transcription and overlap in the audio.

00:00 Speaker 1 (Jordan): alright thanks everyone for joining, quick check - Maya you good to go?
00:07 Speaker 2 (Maya): yes sorry, bit of background noise at my side but all good. we ran the baseline runs overnight per the script you sent.
00:15 Speaker 3 (Priya): perfect, we have the consolidated numbers here, i pulled the raw logs and a simplified sheet, link in the notes: https://redwood-internal.s3/atlas/benchmarks-0407.xlsx
00:28 Speaker 2 (Luis): ok great, high level we care about p95 latency for our low-latency interactive flows and sustained throughput for batch nightly re-ranks.
00:35 Speaker 3 (Priya): yes, so short summary: for the retrieval-augmented generation prompts (avg prompt len ~120 tokens, response ~80 tokens) we see Redwood Gen-2 quantized profile at p95 = 125 ms on the 1k-concurrent synthetic test, baseline provider p95 = ~185 ms under same concurrency.
00:52 Speaker 2 (Maya): wait those are ms? 125 ms p95 sounds really good, are those end-to-end or just inference?
00:58 Speaker 3 (Priya): good question — these are end-to-end from HTTP ingress to last token returned, includes serialization. we also tracked kernel-level time; raw inference-only p95 was ~90 ms on our tuned runtime, baseline inference-only was ~150 ms.
01:16 Speaker 4 (Ethan): throughput wise, in steady-state Redwood sustained ~210 req/s (around 16k tokens/s aggregated), baseline sustained ~140 req/s on the same VM footprint (A100 equivalent). we used continuous batching with a max batch size of 64 for the Redwood runs.
01:33 Speaker 2 (Luis): curious about how you configured batching; we worry about head-of-line latency for small interactive requests.
01:39 Speaker 3 (Priya): right — we used an adaptive batching policy: short tail requests (<64 tokens) allowed immediate flush at 15 ms while background batching accumulated similar requests up to 64. That keeps p50 very low while improving token efficiency for throughput.
01:53 Speaker 2 (Maya): did you enable KV-cache for the multi-turn tests?
01:57 Speaker 3 (Priya): yes KV-cache on for multi-turn scenarios; that reduced token generation by ~20% for your conversational workload which improves cost and latency. we also tried int8 quantization profile — slightly higher variance on edge cases, so we left int8 for the nightly batch where quality tolerance is higher.
02:13 Speaker 2 (Maya): how about cost? baseline was quoting per-1k token at $0.45 for the managed endpoint; your estimate last week was lower but do you have updated numbers given the throughput gains?
02:22 Speaker 1 (Jordan): we ran a nominal costing calc in the sheet — rough ballpark for Atlas workload is $0.30/1k tokens on Redwood hosted with current batching + cache profile; dedicated reserved capacity would change the unit economics, we'll put detailed pricing in the sheet.
02:37 Speaker 2 (Samir): for enterprise we care about data separation and audit logs. can the dedicated option push logs to our splunk and integrate with our KMS?
02:44 Speaker 4 (Ethan): yes, dedicated supports customer-managed KMS, audit logs to S3/splunk, and VPC peering. we'll include the SOC2/architectural diagram in the security package.
02:55 Speaker 2 (Luis): any capacity constraints you saw under the stress runs? we simulated spikes to 2k concurrent.
03:02 Speaker 3 (Priya): above 1.5k concurrency we started to see tail latency increase; though Redwood's smart-routing fell back to a slightly cheaper variant to keep time under SLA — that had slightly higher p95 but still better than baseline. We documented the thresholds in the sheet.
03:18 Speaker 2 (Maya): can you repeat the 95th-percentile test with our real prompt set (not synthetic) to validate?
03:22 Speaker 1 (Jordan): absolutely — next step is Redwood to run 95p tests with the Atlas prompt set and share raw logs.
03:29 Speaker 2 (Maya): also, we noticed a couple transcription errors in last week's notes where model names got swapped — "Gen-2" was transcribed as "Jen-two" — just flagging that for the record.
03:36 Speaker 3 (Priya): thanks; i'll make sure labels are clear. on tuning: two levers we recommend — 1) reduce max batch flush to 32 for interactive routes to improve tail latency by ~12% and 2) enable per-customer prefix caching for the retrieval layer which reduces upstream hits by ~30%.
03:52 Speaker 2 (Luis): sounds good. for the quantization tradeoff, do you have a test harness for quality regression so we can see rouge/bleu or answer fidelity delta?
04:00 Speaker 4 (Ethan): yes we ran an eval set; int8 showed a 0.7% delta on our QA metric for the retrieval use case, int4 had larger regressions in corner cases. we'll share the eval notebook and results link: https://redwood-evals.internal/atlas/0407
04:12 Speaker 2 (Maya): what's the recommended initial pilot config?
04:15 Speaker 3 (Priya): start hosted with reserved pool sized to your peak plus 20% for burst; routes: interactive route with max_batch 32 + adaptive flush 10 ms, nightly batch route with int8 quantization and larger batch sizes. after 2 weeks and baseline validations move to a Dedicated SHARED node set for lower unit costs.
04:34 Speaker 2 (Samir): timeline for security review and procurement?
04:37 Speaker 1 (Jordan): i'll send SOC2 docs and the dedicated pricing sheet today; procurement typically takes 4-6 weeks but we can fast-track once security signoff is done.
04:46 Speaker 2 (Maya): okay recap: Redwood runs 95p tests with our real prompts, send security docs + pricing, Atlas provides final prompt set and success criteria.
04:54 Speaker 1 (Jordan): exactly. any other questions?
05:00 Speaker 2 (Luis): just one: are there specific GPU families you ran on? baseline used A100, what did you run?
05:06 Speaker 3 (Priya): we ran on H100 instances for the primary Redwood results — optimized kernels for that hardware. we also have comparative runs on A100 which are in the sheet.
05:15 Speaker 2 (Maya): perfect. thanks everyone.
05:18 Speaker 1 (Jordan): thanks team, we'll follow up with links and updated sheet.
05:22 Speaker 2 (Maya): thanks, bye.

Notes:
- Artifact links: benchmark spreadsheet (https://redwood-internal.s3/atlas/benchmarks-0407.xlsx), eval notebook (https://redwood-evals.internal/atlas/0407), security deck (link to be shared)
- Observations: Redwood improved p95 by ~30% vs baseline provider under Atlas synthetic load; throughput improved ~50% for same VM footprint; KV-cache and adaptive batching are primary contributors.
- Known issues: int8 showed slight quality variance for a small subset of prompts; tail latency increases above 1.5k concurrency — recommended mitigations provided.
